---
title: "09. Vertical reference specification"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{09. Vertical reference specification}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Analysis setup separates Horizontal CRS and Vertical reference into compact tabs.
The vertical form records the intended Study Area target, not a claim that source
DEMs already conform. Saving never rewrites their declarations or elevation values.

`study_vertical_reference_server()` obtains candidates through
`fluvgeo::study_vertical_crs_candidates()`: nondeprecated upward EPSG height CRSs
from sf's local PROJ database, screened against the Study Area geographic bounds.
Full-bounds coverage is the default; partial overlap is opt-in. Neither proves
actual geographic applicability or transformation accuracy. A reference link lets
the analyst inspect the catalog definition. No default vertical CRS is chosen.

Separate input paths cover standalone vertical CRS, ellipsoidal height with a
3D geographic CRS, declared/future names, local references and unknowns. Height
type and target elevation unit remain explicit. A target unit differing from a
CRS's native axis unit is specification metadata, not an executed conversion.
Coordinate-epoch and intended-model fields are optional disclosures. Known epochs
need a decimal year and scientific source reference; frame epoch and acquisition
date are never substituted. There are no personal Recorded by or generic Why fields.

Check specification calls `fluvgeo::validate_study_vertical_reference()` and binds
the validated row to exact effective inputs and context revision. Unknown/local/
declared choices are retained with an unqualified status; dynamic definitions are
metadata-only and require a future epoch workflow. Editing a checked field or
changing context invalidates saving. The shared pending-edit guard still blocks
real unsaved geometry or acquisition changes.

Save calls `store$set_vertical_reference()` -> `revise()` -> injected
`fluvgeo::set_study_vertical_reference()`. The backend writes schema 7 with a
structured single-row vertical_reference table plus descriptive vertical/unit
analysis_reference rows atomically. Existing processing records require migration
before a target change. The saved callback rereads the new revision, including
the structured table. Renaming, purpose edits and horizontal CRS changes retain
it. Older contexts remain readable; older backend versions reject schema 7.

Validation errors and save confirmation render beside Check/Save. Confirmation
is bound to the saved revision path, so the current-context observer cannot erase
it and a different study cannot inherit it. Reopening fills every stored field;
resolved definitions use their authority identifier where available, otherwise
WKT. Article 01 explains reload restoration from the tab's local study key.
Checking alone is not a save, and unsaved form state is not recovered after reload.

`crs_selectize_options()` is shared by both CRS menus. The dropdown is appended to
the document body, outside clipping card containers. Its list height uses viewport
space and it opens upward when needed. Asynchronous option loads recalculate that
placement. Internal scrolling stays active; scrolling a containing page closes the
menu to avoid a detached overlay. Destroying a control removes its scroll listener.

Source routes: R/study_vertical_reference.R, R/study_analysis_crs.R, R/mod_study.R,
R/study_store.R; backend R/study_vertical_reference.R and R/study_context.R.
Tests: test-study-vertical-reference.R; backend test_study_vertical_reference.R;
dropdown callback fixture: dev/scripts/check-crs-dropdown.cjs. The exact persisted
contract is sibling fluvgeo/dev/schemas/study-vertical-reference.md.

Source-reference reconciliation and transformation qualification are still needed
before mosaicking mixed inputs. Metadata assignment, unit conversion, datum/epoch
transformation and raster resampling remain separate explicit operations.
